senses.def: Since, from (a given time, earlier state etc.).
ex: He hasn't been well of late.

senses.def: From, away from (a position, number, distance etc.).
ex: There are no shops within twenty miles of the cottage.

senses.def: Indicating removal, absence or separation, with the action indicated by a transitive verb and the quality or substance by a grammatical object.
ex: Finally she was relieved of the burden of caring for her sick husband.

senses.def: Indicating removal, absence or separation, with resulting state indicated by an adjective.
ex: He seemed devoid of human feelings.

senses.def: Indicating an ancestral source or origin of descent.
ex: The word is believed to be of Japanese origin.

senses.def: Introducing an epithet that indicates a birthplace, residence, dominion, or other place associated with the individual.
ex: Jesus of Nazareth (after hometown)
Anselm of Canterbury (after diocese)

senses.def: Indicating a (non-physical) source of action or emotion; introducing a cause, instigation; from, out of, as an expression of.
ex: The invention was born of necessity.

senses.def: Indicates the source or cause of the verb.
ex: It is said that she died of a broken heart.

senses.def: Indicates the subject or cause of the adjective.
ex: I am tired of all this nonsense.

senses.def: Indicates the agent (for most verbs, now usually expressed with by).
ex: I am not particularly enamoured of this idea.

senses.def: Used to introduce the “subjective genitive”; following a noun to form the head of a postmodifying noun phrase (see also ‘Possession’ senses below).
ex: The contract can be terminated at any time with the agreement of both parties.

senses.def: Used to indicate the agent of something described by the adjective.
ex: It was very brave of you to speak out like that.

senses.def: Used to indicate the material or substance used.
ex: Many 'corks' are now actually made of plastic.

senses.def: Indicating the composition of a given collective or quantitative noun.
ex: I'll have a dozen of those apples, please.
What a lot of nonsense!

senses.def: Used to link a given class of things with a specific example of that class.
ex: Germany's formal name is the Federal Republic of Germany.
Welcome to the historic town of Harwich.

senses.def: Links two nouns in near-apposition, with the first qualifying the second; “which is also”.
ex: I'm not driving this wreck of a car.

senses.def: Links an intransitive verb, or a transitive verb and its subject (especially verbs to do with thinking, feeling, expressing etc.), with its subject-matter; concerning, with regard to.
ex: I'm always thinking of you.

senses.def: Introduces its subject matter; about, concerning.
ex: He told us the story of his journey to India.

senses.def: Introduces the whole for which is indicated only the specified part or segment; “from among”.
ex: Most of these apples are rotten.

senses.def: Indicates a given part.
ex: We want a larger slice of the cake.

senses.def: Links to a genitive noun or possessive pronoun, with partitive effect (though now often merged with possessive senses, below; see also double possessive).
ex: He is a friend of mine.

senses.def: Belonging to, existing in, or taking place in a given location, place or time. Compare “origin” senses, above.
ex: He was perhaps the most famous scientist of the twentieth century.

senses.def: Belonging to (a place) through having title, ownership or control over it.
ex: The owner of the nightclub was arrested.

senses.def: Belonging to (someone or something) as something they possess or have as a characteristic; the “possessive genitive”. (With abstract nouns, this intersects with the subjective genitive, above under “agency” senses.)
ex: Keep the handle of the saucepan away from the flames.

senses.def: Forming the “objective genitive”.
Follows an agent noun, verbal noun or noun of action.
ex: She had a profound distrust of the police.

senses.def: Indicates a quality or characteristic; “characterized by”.
ex: Pooh was said to be a bear of very little brain.

senses.def: Indicates quantity, age, price, etc.
ex: A young man of 20 has been paying interest at an exorbitant rate of 10%.

senses.def: Used to link singular indefinite nouns (preceded by the indefinite article) and attributive adjectives modified by certain common adverbs of degree.
ex: It's not that big of a deal. (Standard form: It's not that big a deal.)

senses.def: During the course of (a set period of time, day of the week etc.), now specifically with implied repetition or regularity.
ex: Of an evening, we would often go for a stroll along the river.

senses.def: For (a given length of time).
ex: I’ve not taken her out of a goodly long while.

senses.def: Indicates duration of a state, activity etc.
ex: After a delay of three hours, the plane finally took off.

senses.def: Before (the hour); to (the hour).
ex: I’ll be ready at ten of two
What's the time? / Nearly a quarter of three.

senses.def: Often used without the hour.
ex: I’ll be ready at ten of
